about: Ringshadow's own shared and base sounds: what a driven unit hears (step = footfall of a unit on foot, breath = its laboured breath in the helmet below a third of its health, lockon = a target coming into reach under the sight, hitmark / hitclank / killmark = its round striking a unit / a building / killing, in your ear; levelup = the driven kind going up a level, pick = a leveling pick kept, both in your ear; dirthit = a miss striking the ground where the sight meets it), boom = a building going up, hum = the Citadel's idle loop (the game loops only the first file), wind = the ambient bed (one seamless loop; the game layers it with a copy offset by half), alert = the Oracle warning that blue's base is under attack (at most every 30 s, in your ear). The Oracle ("Autocraft Oracle", made with Voice Design, eleven_ttv_v3) is the base's computer: calm, even and clearly synthetic, the flattest intonation of the roster; its lines go through Oracle.py (wide band, a faint synthetic sheen, no radio squelch), not comm.py. Ids match the game's sound names (sfx/<name>_<n>); the markers and footfalls are trimmed short (trim.py) since they fire several times a second.

entries.text: [calm, even] Warning. The base is taking fire.
[flat, precise] Alert. Hostile fire on base structures.
[calm, clinical] Attention. Our buildings are under fire.
